To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
total variation minimization can reconstruct images stably and robustly from O(s log N) measurements and this number of measurements is near-optimal.

total variation minimization can be used to reconstruct a signal to within the best k-term approximation of its derivative from O(s log(n)) linear measurements and that this result can be extended to the case of non-adaptive measurements.

the total variation of a signal is the sum of the total variation of its best s-term approximation and the total variation of the difference, and that the difference is the gradient of a function in a null space that can be characterized by a strengthened Sobolevic inequality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: given a signal that is sparse in a known transform, can we reconstruct it from a small number of noisy measurements?
the following problem.
the recovery of images from a small number of measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
from O(s) nonadaptive linear measurements of an image, its gradient can be stably recovered to within the best gradient of its s-term approximation.

, given a noisy image of a piecewise constant function, it is possible to recover a piecewise constant image with the same piecewise constants, up to an additive error of O(1/s), from O(s log(s)) noisy linear measurements, provided the measurements are taken from a matrix that is incoherent with the null space of the image.

, given an image f and a set of measurements y, we can recover the gradient of f to within a factor of 1 + O(1/s) of the best s-term gradient approximation of f up to a factor of O(1/s log(N)) with probability 1 - O(1/N) provided that we have O(s log(N) log(N)) measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that total variation minimization can recover the true image from a very small number of measurements with a very low error rate.
we show that total variation minimization is a stable, robust and efficient image reconstruction algorithm.
we show that the null space of an incoherent matrix is close to a Sobolev space, in the sense that the null space is close to the intersection of the Sobolev space with the null space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the common belief that nonadaptive linear measurements are insufficient for stable image reconstruction, total variation minimization is surprisingly robust and stable to such measurements.
, in the context of total variation regularization, a small amount of incoherence between the measurements and the image can go a long way in stabilizing the image recovery process.
total variation regularization is a powerful tool for image recovery, even from very few and noisy measurements.
